name: BattleResumeImage
summary: The payload of a resume entry of `autoenhanced.png`. Two forms: the world and main entries carry the 40,164-byte save work copy (the manual-slot layout) at +356 behind a 340-byte header; the attack and fturn entries, and the battle main entry, carry a 668,112-byte battle snapshot followed by a fixed 1 MB texture page. The two headers and the texture section are in ResumeEntry; the snapshot's blocks are in BattleSnapshot.

members.name: file_header
members.text: same shape as the manual-save header: u32 16 at +0, a changing u32 at +4, u32 17 at +8, u32 0 at +12

members.name: tag
members.text: `FFTI`

members.name: header_word
members.text: 122 (0x7A) in every entry decoded

members.name: payload_size
members.text: 40508 for a world entry; equals entry length - 16

members.name: reserved
members.text: all 0xFF in the world entries

members.name: work_copy
members.text: a packed save work copy with the manual-slot layout; 882 bytes differ from manual slot 0 of the same save set

members.name: trailer
members.text: zero

behavior.text: the owner's `autoenhanced.png` decodes to 16 entries: `resume_en00..02_{world,attack,fturn,main}.sav`, `resume_enbtl_{world,attack,main}.sav` and `resume_enwm_main.sav`.

decoded lengths: world entries 40524 bytes; `resume_en00_attack.sav` 1101050; `resume_en00_fturn.sav` 1078129; `resume_en00_main.sav` 1077019; `resume_en01_main.sav` 1074514; `resume_en02_main.sav` 1076987; `resume_enbtl_main.sav` 1078129.
every world entry has `SC` at +356; the 40164 bytes there compare with manual slot 0 with only 882 differing bytes.
those differing bytes are the summary, date and situation fields a later pack would change.
the later save-time copy of the same layout is what `SaveSlot_LoadToLive` loads when the slot's situation byte is 1.
the 356-byte prefix is a resume descriptor (scene, entry kind and the time token); its fields are not decoded.
the main/attack/fturn images hold the battle state proper (a 66-byte learned block was matched inside a main entry); their internal layout is not decoded.
whether the main/attack/fturn image carries a copy of the random state, the frame counters or the camera record.

notes: The world entry does carry the slot work copy; it starts at +356, not at a different layout. The container itself is a PNG `ffTo` chunk, `UMIF`, XOR scramble and preset-dictionary deflate.
open_questions: ? what the game does when a requested resume entry is absent; ? which scene event marks each of the resume points 00..02; ? the meaning of the 16 battle control words.

name: ItemHelpToken
summary: The 0x6800-tagged text id that asks for an item's help string: kind 13, index = item id. Five functions build it at six sites, with three index masks (0x3FF, 0x7FF, a runtime register) or none, and store it in the shared help slot 0x1418736B4; a sixth function only bounds a script operand at 0x105. It is a pool id, not the Item-en description the equipment detail panel uses.

members.name: token
members.text: 0x6800 + item id: the tag is added at the builder and the id becomes the low 11 bits.

members.name: kind
members.text: 13 (0x6800 >> 11): the item help pool.

members.name: index
members.text: The item id. The builders mask it with 0x3FF (two sites), 0x7FF (one), a runtime register (one) or not at all (two).

members.name: help_slot
members.text: The shared help slot 0x1418736B4; 32 dword stores exist in the code. Its three readers are a compare, a sign-extended render command and the adder of 0x7800 / 0x9800. The u16 at +4 is a separate field.

behavior.text: the token is built at six sites in five functions: sub_1402D58EC, sub_1402D5FE4, sub_140301ED8, sub_140333974 (two sites) and sub_1403343E4. A seventh 0x6800 site, in sub_1403015A4, only bounds a script operand.
the event-script builder sub_140301ED8 passes 0x6800 + (operand & 0x7FF) to the generic decoder; the script builder sub_1403015A4 only compares an operand with 0x6800 and bounds its index at 0x105.
ids from 0x800 up do not stay item help: 0x6800 + N becomes 0x7000, the ability kind, and the decoder answers it from the ability name source.
the equipment detail panel does not use this token: EquipDetail_SetHelpText reads the Item-en row's description field (column +16) directly.
the pool 13 strings are the item help entries; the pool content was not read.

notes: V: the help slot is shared with the job and command help paths, which load it with 0x7800 or 0x9800 ids (sub_140366FE0 adds those tags to a stored index), so a reader cannot take kind 13 from the slot alone.
open_questions: ? the exact string a token names versus the Item-en description; ? which screens show the token rather than the row description.

name: ItemIconPath
summary: The two per-item picture paths: a detail picture (Icon table row 12) and a list picture (row 13), both formatted from the item id and both texture-parts URIs. The number is the item id with %03d as a minimum width; nothing masks it. Each path names a part file that in turn names its texture.

members.name: detail
members.text: equip_item/textureparts/ei_%03d_uitx, prefixed with the UITextureParts scheme and ui/ffto/icon/ by Icon_FormatPath. Used by the equipment detail panel and the detail views.

members.name: list
members.text: equip_item_s/textureparts/ei_s_%03d_uitx, with the same prefix. Used by list cells (shop rows, item lists).

members.name: id_field
members.text: The item id, minimum width 3: 1 gives ei_001, 1000 gives ei_1000, 65535 gives ei_65535. The id is a 32-bit argument with no mask or truncation in the formatters; the caller's buffer cap is the only limit.

members.name: scheme
members.text: The UITextureParts scheme, followed by ui/ffto/icon/; this is the texture-parts mode of Icon_FormatPath, selected by both item formatters.

members.name: buffer
members.text: 0x104 (260) inside both formatters; the six callers pass 0x100 or 0x104. Str_Format truncates at the cap and no caller checks the result.

members.name: pair
members.text: Each path names a .utexpt part file; the part file carries the path of the .tex texture. The retail packs hold 261 detail textures (100 x 100, BC7) and 261 list textures (48 x 48, BC7), ids 0..260.

behavior.text: id <= 0 formats as 0 (the formatters replace a non-positive id with 0).
the id is not the record's icon field: the record's two icon bytes feed the classic tile path (ItemIcon_Set), while these paths are named by the id alone.

a missing file is not detected at bind time: ItemCell_BindIconAndName binds the path when the Item-en name row exists and the id is not negative, without checking that the part file or the texture exists.
the UI looks a texture part up by path inside the mounted packs (lower-cased, separators normalised).

notes: V: six call sites in six functions: two large (sub_140109134, EquipDetail_Refresh) and four small (sub_140142014, sub_14014D57C, sub_140153CA0, ItemCell_SetItem). The text-id site inside sub_140153CA0 feeds the 11-bit item id of a 0x3800 cell, so it inherits the text-id limit.
open_questions: ? what the screen shows when the part file exists but the texture does not (the size fallback is 1 x 1; the pixels were not observed).

name: ManualSaveEntry
summary: The `fftsave.bin` entry of `enhanced.png` (and of `classic.png`): one flat image of the 50-slot save cache, 50 x 40,164 bytes behind a 16-byte header. There is no per-slot file and no per-slot write: a save, a delete and an import all rewrite the whole image.

members.name: header
members.type: {uint32 header_size; uint32 crc32; uint32 version; uint32 reserved}
members.text: Header size 16, CRC-32 over the 50-slot payload, version 14, reserved 0.

members.name: slots
members.text: One 40,164-byte (0x9CE4) slot per index; slot n starts at +16 + 40,164 n.

members.name: magic
members.text: `SC`: a slot that starts with this pair is used; any other slot is skipped by the load list.

members.name: summary_job
members.text: The leader's job byte as the load list shows it.

members.name: summary_level
members.text: The leader's level.

members.name: place
members.text: The place byte the list shows.

members.name: situation
members.text: 1 marks a slot saved in battle; loading such a slot also requests its resume entry.

members.name: unit_records
members.text: 54 records of 600 bytes, the same layout the live table g_UnitSaveData holds (see UnitSaveRecord).

members.name: total
members.text: The decoded entry length; a reader that finds another length rejects the whole image.

behavior.text: the store copies the 50-slot cache into the manager image and queues this entry with version 14; the PNG write is requested separately on the request object, in the same frame step.
the load first fills the image with the empty-slot pattern and then requests the entry, so a missing or rejected payload leaves 50 empty slots rather than stale ones.
the payload handler checks the CRC and, for version 14, the exact size; on a mismatch it zeroes the image and returns an error (there is no per-slot recovery).
a delete is a slot rewrite (the slot is filled with 0xFF) followed by the same whole-image store; no separate record is removed.
`classic.png` uses the same entry and the same image, but its list maps index 0 to the 51st auto slot g_SaveAutoSlot and shifts the cache by one.
every backup slot read from real save files was reproduced as a 40,164-byte slot byte for byte, which is the practical check of this layout.

notes: The slot's own fields (summary, sprite records, unit table, item and errand tables) are described in UnitSaveRecord and in the save schema records; this page covers the entry envelope and the anchors needed to place a slot.
open_questions: ? the spare bytes at the end of a slot image (0xFF in a used slot).

name: NxdMultiKeyIndex
summary: The index of a double or triple keyed nxd file (header byte 8 = 2 or 3): sets by key1, per set an array (double) or children by key2 with their leaves (triple), and one flat entry table of every row sorted by the key tuple. The rows, strings and arrays are encoded as in a single-key file.

members.name: kind
members.text: 2 double keyed (layout byte +9 = 3 or 4), 3 triple keyed (+9 = 5 or 6); 52 and 6 retail files.

members.name: sets_contiguous
members.text: Double keyed: set only when the set keys are first_key, first_key + 1, ... (17 of the 52 files); the game does not read it for these kinds (BindRows reads +10 only for layouts 1 and 2).

members.name: first_key
members.text: The first set key when +10 is set, else 0.

members.name: sets
members.text: The set table, offset relative to +32 (60 double, 56 triple in every retail file); the walkers take the address file + 32.

members.name: entries3
members.text: Triple: the flat entry table at this ABSOLUTE offset and its count (BindRows binds one entry per record).

members.name: entries2
members.text: Double: the flat entry table at this ABSOLUTE offset, count at +48.

members.name: set2
members.text: 12 bytes, sorted by key1 (binary search NxdSets_Find2); array offset relative to the record; empty sets exist (usersituation: 10).

members.name: entry2
members.text: 12 bytes, row offset relative to the record; an array is sorted by key2; NxdEntry_GetRow (kind 2) adds +8.

members.name: set3
members.type: {uint32 key1; int32 children; int32 count; int32 leaves; int32 zero}
members.text: 20 bytes, sorted by key1 (NxdSets_Find3); children offset relative to the record; the set-level leaf count is 0 in every retail file (its offset is not read with count 0).

members.name: child3
members.type: {uint32 key2; int32 offset; int32 zero; int32 leaves; int32 count}
members.text: 20 bytes, sorted by key2 (NxdSet3_FindChild); leaves at +12 relative to the child, count +16; +4 equals +12 and +8 is 0 in every retail file (a walker descends while +8 is positive).

members.name: entry3
members.type: {uint32 key1; uint32 key2; uint32 key3; int32 zero; int32 row}
members.text: 20 bytes, row offset relative to the record at +16; leaves sorted by key3; +12 is 0 everywhere; NxdEntry_GetRow (kind 3) adds +16.

behavior.text: in every retail file the arrays (double) or leaves (triple), concatenated in set order, are exactly the flat entry table (keys and row offsets), sorted by the key tuple; the game relies on it: NxdTable_GetSetEntries returns the entry of a set's first record and a count that its callers step through as consecutive bound entries.

a lookup by keys searches the flat entries (NxdEntries_Search2 / 3); a lookup by key1 and position goes through the set, takes that record's keys and then searches the flat entries (NxdTable_GetEntryByKeyIndex): the array record's own row offset is not used by these paths.
retail layout order: header, set table, per set its array (or children and leaves) followed by that set's rows, the flat entry table, the string pool. Only the offsets matter to the game.

all 58 files decode with these invariants checked (every set, array and leaf is walked and compared with the flat table); 49 double and 5 triple keyed tables decode row for row against every stock row (15,372 and 6,451 rows).

open_questions: ? layouts 4 and 6 versus 3 and 5 (the English text tables use 4; BindRows treats 3/4 and 5/6 alike; no file with layout 6).

name: NxdSingleKeyHeader
summary: The header bytes of an nxd file that the game's loader (NxdTable_BindRows) reads for a single-key table, and the contiguous-keys flag that decides whether a key is read by position or searched.

members.name: magic
members.text: 'NXDF'.

members.name: mode
members.text: 1 for single-key tables (entry kind 1: the row is the entry pointer plus the dword at +4).

members.name: layout
members.text: 1 or 2: single key, row count at +36; 3 or 4: count at +48; 5 or 6: count at +44.

members.name: contiguous_keys
members.text: Not 0: row i holds key first_key + i, and the game reads row (key - first_key) instead of searching. Retail files set it only when that is true.

members.name: first_key
members.text: The key of row 0 when +10 is set; 0 in every retail file without the flag.

members.name: rows_offset
members.text: Offset of the row table: 8 bytes per row, the key (uint32) first, sorted by key.

members.name: row_count
members.text: Number of rows (layouts 1 and 2).

name: NxdSingleKeyRows
summary: The row area of a single-key nxd file (header byte 8 = 1, byte 9 = 1 or 2): the entry table, the rows and the string pool, and how a row refers to its strings and arrays. Completes NxdSingleKeyHeader.

members.name: entries
members.text: One per row, ascending keys; the row starts at the entry's own address + rel (NxdEntry_GetRow, kind 1).

members.name: rows
members.text: Each row: its fixed part (the columns in layout order, each aligned to min(size, 4), rounded up to 4), then that row's arrays.

members.name: string pool
members.text: NUL-terminated UTF-8 strings; an empty string stands for a null cell (27,103 such cells checked).

members.name: integer / float column
members.text: Little endian, in place.

members.name: string column
members.text: Target minus a base: the row start, or for the relative columns the column's own position plus the layout's adjustment (Item: every name column relative to row +4).

members.name: array column
members.text: Elements at row start + offset; an empty array keeps an offset and count 0.

members.name: union column
members.text: A _uniontypes id and a row id.

members.name: string array column
members.text: int32 elements at row start + offset, each a string offset relative to the ARRAY start (8 layout columns, every row checked).

members.name: struct array column
members.text: Elements of the struct's size (members placed like columns, size rounded up to 4) at row start + offset; a string member is relative to its ELEMENT start (4 layout columns, every row checked).

behavior.text: every reference inside the row area is relative (to the entry, the row or the column), so the whole area can move as one block.
186 of the 188 single-key retail files decode with this column order and alignment, checked against every stock row (all 32,752 rows, every column).
the same row encoding holds in the double / triple keyed files (NxdMultiKeyIndex); only the index differs.

a layout can be longer than the rows: OverrideEntryData's layout ends at +0x9D (row size 160) but its rows are 156 bytes apart, so its last column is the next row's first byte (OverrideEntry_FillUnitEntry reads up to +0x99). A byte check against the stock rows cannot see this.

notes: The byte check against every stock row is what makes the column order and types V for these files.
open_questions: ? why one RefinedBgTexture row (71 2 0) has string-array elements pointing into the next row (the offset field of its Comment): an artefact of the tool that wrote the file (I).

name: ResumeEntry
summary: One entry of `autoenhanced.png`: a 16-byte entry header, a 340-byte payload header, then a body that is either the 40,164-byte save work copy (kind 0, the world and main form) or a 668,112-byte battle snapshot followed by a fixed 1 MB texture page (kind 1). Completes BattleResumeImage, which describes the payload bodies; this page gives the two headers and the texture section. Offsets below are from the start of the entry.

members.name: entry_header
members.type: {uint32 size; uint32 crc32; uint32 version; uint32 reserved}
members.text: 16, CRC-32 of the payload, 17, 0; the CRC is compared when the entry is attached to its object.

members.name: magic
members.text: `FFTI`; a payload with another tag is rejected by the import.

members.name: version
members.text: 122 (0x7A); any other value is rejected.

members.name: structured_size
members.text: 40,508 for kind 0 or 786,776 for kind 1: the size of the structured payload, not the entry length (a kind-1 entry is longer by its texture section).

members.name: kind
members.text: 0 = save work copy (world and main entries), 1 = battle (attack and fturn, and the battle main entry).

members.name: self_check
members.text: 70 (0x46) times the structured size; the import recomputes the product from the tag's first byte and the size field and rejects a mismatch.

members.name: leader_name
members.text: Blank in every decoded entry; the import copies 17 bytes (with the next byte) into the auto slot's name field.

members.name: summary_tag
members.text: 0xFE, the empty-name marker the manual slot summary also carries.

members.name: summary_job
members.text: The first party unit's job byte.

members.name: summary_level
members.text: The first party unit's level.

members.name: place_bytes
members.text: Two scene variables read after a scene update; they become the slot summary's two place bytes.

members.name: place_id
members.text: Scene variable 0x31, the map/place byte.

members.name: party_index
members.text: The leader's party slot (1 when the party object is absent).

members.name: cleared
members.text: Game-cleared flag, copied into the summary.

members.name: global_byte
members.text: A global byte copied into the header but not read back by the import.

members.name: config_byte
members.text: A config byte (the difficulty), copied into the summary.

members.name: battle_marker
members.text: Set when kind is 1; the materialiser branches on it.

members.name: new_game_plus
members.text: New-game+ flag, copied into the summary.

members.name: reserved_at_40
members.text: Zero.

members.name: play_time
members.text: Hours x 3600 + minutes x 60 + seconds, from the three clock bytes at 0x141856700.

members.name: timestamp
members.text: Time of the capture; the import puts it at slot +68.

members.name: progress
members.text: Main progress value, copied into the summary.

members.name: previews
members.text: Six 32-byte preview records for kind 0 only (the leader, then units 50..53); the resume list draws its sprites from them.

members.name: reserved_at_114
members.text: Zero.

members.name: battle_control
members.text: Three battle control words; the materialiser copies them back to the globals they came from (0x142E7FC78 and two more).

members.name: battle_words
members.text: Sixteen more battle control words (0x142E7FEA0).

members.name: body
members.text: Kind 0: the 40,164-byte work copy, then 4 zero bytes. Kind 1: the 668,112-byte snapshot, then 118,324 zero bytes.

members.name: yox_magic
members.text: `YOX` and a zero byte, at the end of the structured size; kind 1 only.

members.name: yox_codec
members.text: 2 = deflate, 0 = stored (the writer falls back when compression fails).

members.name: yox_raw_size
members.text: 1,048,576: the inflated page has a fixed size.

members.name: yox_data
members.text: Inflates into the fixed 1 MB page, a 1024 x 512 16-bpp image; it carries no object id.

behavior.text: two saved backups hold 16 entries: `resume_en00..02_{main,world,attack,fturn}`, `resume_enbtl_{main,world,attack}` and `resume_enwm_main`; the battle set has no fturn entry.
kind 0 is a manual-slot work copy byte for byte, only shifted (body at entry +356, which is slot +0); main and world entries differ in name and summary, not in form.
kind 1 is a sparse same-build memory snapshot (41.5 to 54.7 KB of its 668,112 bytes are nonzero) followed by 118,324 zero bytes, so the structured size stays the constant 786,776.
the texture page follows the structured size and is not counted in it; the attack and fturn captures carry different pages, so it must be stored byte exact.
the queue function stamps the CRC and queues with version 17, and the import verifies the self-check product before it copies the summary into the auto slot.
the 340-byte header is a union of a resume summary and battle control words, because a kind-0 entry fills only the summary half and the kind-1 entries add the battle block.

notes: BattleResumeImage gives the payload forms, BattleSnapshot the blocks of the kind-1 body, and UnitSaveRecord the fields of the work copy. Entry lengths follow from the forms: 40,524 for kind 0 and 1,119,315 in the observed kind-1 copy.
open_questions: ? the meaning of the 16 battle control words beyond the globals they are copied to; ? what the game does when a requested resume entry is absent.

name: SavePngContainer
summary: A game save file: an ordinary PNG whose private `ffTo` chunk carries a `UMIF` container. Each entry is scrambled and then deflated against a fixed 32 KB dictionary held in the executable, so a reader needs the container walk, the scramble and that dictionary. The file name is the area name (`ENHANCED`, `AUTOENHANCED`, `SYSTEM`, `CLASSIC`) plus `.png`; manual slots, resume entries and the settings block all travel in this one shape.

members.name: png_signature
members.text: The standard PNG signature; the chunk walk starts at +8.

members.name: chunk_tag
members.text: Chunks are walked in order (length, tag, data, CRC). The save body is the private chunk tagged `ffTo`; the other chunks are skipped.

members.name: container_tag
members.text: `UMIF`, the container tag; a body with another tag is rejected as not a game save.

members.name: entry_count
members.text: Number of entries; the table starts at body +16.

members.name: entry_record
members.type: {uint32 name_len; uint32 data_len; uint64 name_offset; uint64 raw_len; uint64 data_offset}
members.text: One 32-byte record per entry; the dword at +12 of the record has no reader.

members.name: entry_name
members.text: The name, scrambled like the data and trimmed of trailing NULs: `fftsave.bin`, `settings.sav`, `resume_*_*.sav`.

members.name: entry_data
members.text: Unscrambled, its first 4 bytes are a dictionary id and the rest is deflate data; `raw_len` is the exact inflated size, and a different size is an error.

members.name: preset_dictionary
members.text: The fixed deflate dictionary in the executable's read-only data (its Adler-32 id 0x4DAFCB9C matches the header the inflater builds). It is never stored in the file.

behavior.text: the scramble is its own inverse: 8-byte blocks are XORed with one 64-bit key, a 4-byte tail with the key's low half, and 2- and 1-byte tails with complement-and-mask rules (SaveData_Scramble).
the stored stream is raw deflate with the zlib header left out; the inflater writes a header with the dictionary flag, applies the 32 KB dictionary and checks the deflate stream's own Adler-32.
the entry's own version decides the payload layout (14 for the manual slot image, 0 for the settings block, 17 for a resume entry); the container carries no version of its own.
the container writer re-reads the file it is about to replace, keeps every entry it was not asked to queue, rebuilds the whole container and writes it, so an outside entry survives a vanilla save.
the folder is created by the game at boot and the file is found by area name in the profile's save folder; a missing area file is treated as no save data, not as an error.

notes: Entry-level layouts are in ManualSaveEntry (version 14) and ResumeEntry (version 17); the settings block is option state and is not covered here.
open_questions: ? the 8 bytes at the start of the `ffTo` body, before the container tag; ? the dword at +12 of an entry record; ? the other chunk tags a writer of this build can emit besides `ffTo`.

name: SpriteSheetEntries
summary: The sprite data of a unit look: two HD sheet entries, the classic sprite file and its palette rows.

members.name: sheet rows 0..511
members.text: The first HD sheet entry as the game holds it inflated: 4 bits per pixel (131072 bytes, low nibble = left pixel), or 8 bits per pixel (262144 bytes) for the sheet groups the battle layer builds with 256 colours. Pixel = colour number, 0 transparent.

members.name: sheet rows 512..975
members.text: The second entry: 118784 bytes at 4 bits, 237568 bytes at 8 bits.

members.name: classic sprite file
members.text: The classic file: its first 0x200 bytes are 16 rows of 16 colours (u16, 5 bits red, green, blue from the low bit). These rows are what the game loads, tints and fades.

behavior.text: the sheets are the classic 256 x 488 sheet drawn at twice the size; which rectangles of it a frame uses comes from the frame files.

name: tec
summary: Shader technique file (for example uirender.tec): the DXBC shader containers of a technique, its programs, sampler presets and the binding tables that tie each shader's registers to engine names.

members.name: shader containers
members.text: Complete DXBC containers at fixed offsets (the shader names on this site use the offset).

members.name: binding records
members.text: One record per bound resource: register (byte), resource class (byte: 0 constant buffer or sampler, 0x54 texture, 0x14 UAV), name offset into the string pool (16-bit). Read from uirender.tec; the record layout is not confirmed by the loader code.

members.name: string pool
members.text: NUL-terminated names: sampler presets (ccc_lln_sampler, ...), constant buffers (cUIRender, cSDF, ...), textures (tTexture0, tTexture1), samplers (g_Sampler, g_Sampler_tMaskBuffer), uav, cCommon, cConstant0.

open_questions: ? the header and the program / permutation tables; the loader that parses the binding records.

name: TextId
summary: A 16-bit text id in two fields: the top 5 bits select one of 32 string pools, the low 11 bits index the strings inside that pool. The single decoder sub_140226208 returns the string pointer; kinds 14 and 22 are redirected before the pool is used. Item names and item help are two different pools: 0x3800 is item text (kind 7), 0x6800 is item help (kind 13).

members.name: kind
members.text: Selects the pool through the 32-entry table qword_140D40990. 0x3800 is kind 7 (item text), 0x6800 kind 13 (item help), 0x7000 kind 14 (ability name).

members.name: index
members.text: String index inside the pool; an index of 0 returns the pool base. The decoder masks the word with 0x7FF and walks that many record separators.

members.name: pool_table
members.text: qword_140D40990: one base per kind. Slot 0 is the event-script text block, written at load by EventScript_LoadIntoBuffer; slots 1..31 are filled by one loop from the text pack at qword_14375F8F0 (base = pack + 0x80 + dword[pack + 4 x kind]). The table is zero in the image.

members.name: strings
members.text: Terminated records separated by byte 0xFE (0xFF counts as a separator too). The walk keeps no end pointer and no length.

members.name: overrides
members.text: Kind 14 is answered by the ability name source sub_140332B48 with argument 2; kind 22 (0xB000) is redirected through sub_1402BACCC(9) to the pool at qword_14375F938 instead of its table entry.

behavior.text: kind = (word >> 11) & 0x1F; index = word & 0x7FF; the base comes from qword_140D40990[kind].

index 0 returns the pool base; a non-zero index counts bytes of 0xFE and above and returns the start of the index-th record. Neither an end pointer nor a length is kept, so an index past the pool runs into the next one.
slot 0 is written by EventScript_LoadIntoBuffer and slots 1..31 by one loop in sub_140301ED8 from the pack at qword_14375F8F0, so every kind has a base at run time.
the pools are per-category string lists; their content was not read (the table is zero in the image).

the 16-bit packing is the wall. 0x3800 + N with N >= 0x800 changes the kind (N = 0x800 gives kind 8, base 0x4000), and 0x6800 + N with N >= 0x800 becomes 0x7000, the ability kind. A wider id needs a different carrier, not a different mask.
the tag helper sub_140220E10 maps a format selector byte to a tag: 0xE9 adds 0x3800, 0xEA adds 0x7000, 0xEB leaves the id bare, 0xE5 adds 0x9000.

three other id spaces are easy to confuse with it: the battle message id (1000 x kind + (word & 0x7FF), table 172), the scene message word (5-bit group + 11-bit index) and the battle message entry kind (a dword per entry).

notes: V: the 32 kinds are in registry TextIdKinds, with the base and the observed producers of each. V: the item name has a second, pool-free route: ItemTable_GetName reads the Item-en row (nxd table 45) by a full 32-bit key, and the equipment detail panel's help is that row's description field, not a 0x6800 token.
open_questions: ? which string each of the 32 pools holds at run time; ? whether a stock index can run past its pool (the walk has no end pointer).

name: TexturePartFile
summary: The part file that names the texture a UI image part shows (ui/ffto/icon/<kind>/textureparts/<name>.utexpt).

members.name: path_offset
members.text: 0x20: where the texture path starts.

members.name: type_name_size
members.text: 12: the length of 'TexturePart' with its terminator.

members.name: type_name_offset
members.text: Offset of the type name from this field: 0x20 + path length (with terminator) - 12.

members.name: reserved
members.text: Zero in every file read.

members.name: size
members.text: 0x30, 0x30: the icon area (48 x 48) of a 60 x 60 job icon texture.

members.name: texture_path
members.text: Terminated path of the texture, e.g. the job icon texture of that index.

members.name: type_name
members.text: 'TexturePart', terminated.

behavior.text: a file built from this layout equals the retail job icon part files j_020 and j_003 byte for byte.

notes: V (header of the stock ei_001 part file): the dword at +0 is 0x20 and the texture path starts at +0x20. V: the dword at +0x0C is the offset of the part-name string relative to +0x0C: 0x44 in ei_001, so the string starts at 0x50; 0x48 in ei_s_123, whose longer equip_item_s path pushes the name four bytes further. V: both files hold one part (count 1 at +0x08), are 0x5C and 0x60 bytes long, and name the literal TexturePart. V: the same header values repeat across the six ei_000..ei_005 files and the four ei_s_120..ei_s_123 files read.
open_questions: ? Whether the game loads a part file that no retail pack has.
